approved: Education Legislation Amendment (2022 Measures No. 1) Bill 2022
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would change the rules for Commonwealth higher education funding and student loans.
It would require students to provide a unique student identifier to their university and the government to be eligible for financial help.
The bill would also remove a 10 per cent discount for upfront HECS-HELP payments and exempt FEE-HELP loan fees for units studied in 2022.
Require students to have and give a unique student identifier to their provider and the Secretary to get Commonwealth assistance.
Clarify that enabling course units do not count towards a student's lifetime limit on Commonwealth support.
Make domestic students in microcredential courses eligible for FEE-HELP.
Reduce FEE-HELP debt by exempting the loan fee for units studied in 2022.
Limit HECS-HELP and FEE-HELP eligibility for New Zealand citizens to those resident in Australia for the unit's duration.
Remove the 10 per cent discount for upfront HECS-HELP payments.
Higher education students, providers, and New Zealand citizens studying in Australia.
Education Legislation Amendment (2022 Measures No. 1) Act 2022
